containment.bound: the realm's own span, not the tenure: the archive does not know the year this place passed to it
containment.why: the archive holds this containment; see the record's notes

notes: drawn on the vector spec's TA plate, which its Section 0 calls Third Age Middle-earth

held under two keys until they were folded: Fornost Erain, Norbury of the Kings, IS Fornost. One record has the city and the coordinate, the other the ruin it became; the place was both, in that order. [I-H]

The North-kingdom's last capital; the great battle that broke Angmar was fought west of it, on the plain between Nenuial and the North Downs (App A I(iv), undated there) and is dated 1975 by App B — App A gives only 1974, the year Angmar TOOK Fornost.
within the Arthedain boundary as the living map draws it, T.A. 861–1974 [I-M]
the vector spec also lists it as “Fornost”, at the same place; one record, not two

timeline.cite: App B, the Tale of Years [C] — '861 Death of Eärendur, and division of Arnor'. App A carries the narrative of the division; App B carries the year. The annal names the EVENT and none of the detail this record gives.
timeline.what: Amlaith, eldest son of Eärendur, holds Fornost and the west

timeline.cite: App B, the Tale of Years [C] — both ends annalled: '1409 The Witch-king of Angmar invades Arnor' and '1974 End of the North-kingdom. The Witch-king overruns Arthedain and takes Fornost'.
timeline.what: The long Angmar war: Amon Sûl burned (1409); the Great Plague (1636); Fornost falls (1974); Arvedui drowns in Forochel (1975)
Fornost taken — then the realm annihilated by Eärnil's host and Glorfindel: 'not a man nor an orc of that realm remained west of the Mountains'
Fall of Arthedain; Battle of Fornost; Angmar broken
